knowledge_point.title: Finding a Unit Vector Parallel to a Given Vector

question.:question/problem: The vector $\overrightarrow{AB}$ has magnitude $30$. Which of the following is a unit vector that is parallel to $\overrightarrow{AB}$?
question.:question/worked-solution:
To obtain the unit vector that is parallel to $\overrightarrow{AB}$, we divide $\overrightarrow{AB}$ by its length:

$$
\mathbf{u}=\dfrac{\overrightarrow{AB}}{\mid \,\overrightarrow{AB}\, \mid}=\dfrac{1}{30}\overrightarrow{AB}
$$

question.:question/problem: The vector $\mathbf{a}$ has magnitude $5 \sqrt{19}$. Find a unit vector that is parallel to $\mathbf{a}$.
question.:question/worked-solution:
To obtain the unit vector that is parallel to $\mathbf{a}$, we divide $\mathbf{a}$ by its length:

$$
\mathbf{u}=\dfrac{\mathbf{a}}{\mid \,\mathbf{a}\, \mid}=\dfrac{1}{5 \sqrt{19}}\mathbf{a}=\frac{\sqrt{19}}{95}\mathbf{a}
$$
